name: Touhou Bansho Cards
summary: 东方题材的 roguelike 卡牌构筑游戏，2026 年 10 月 26 日上架，EskiNott Game Studio 自行开发与发行，分类为冒险／休闲／独立／角色扮演／策略。商店 AI 披露写明生成式 AI 用于美术制作中的图像生成与图像增强，并用于翻译本地化内容。本站据此把美术与翻译登记为已使用，其余六个领域登记为披露未说明。所有结论只有开发者自述支撑，未经独立审计。

sources.label: Question for dev, about the extend of the AI art usage
sources.excerpt:
While I am not pleased entirely with the AI art usage, I do understand the circumstances. As a beginner artist myself, I am slightly disappointed in that that, since there are some elements, particularly CGs, which I found really good looking, beautiful even . Were different AI models used for the art production? Because I particularly found strange that the art is very presentable and it does not at least at first glance anyway, have the usual trappings of AI image generation. I had been enjoying the game, so I am not here to throw unnecessary hate, I just want more information in regards to this. Though it is obvious, thanks to elements being different in artstyle visually, AI was used. I am rather critical of this, no matter the game, because visual incohesion is something I am able to notice and in some cases, it can actually hinder my enjoyment of a particular title. I also had seen the comments and I think it is admirable that the dev is going to work on their artistic skills so they can avod this in the future. Again, as someone who is learning how to draw, I am in full support of this decision. Thank you very much for the answer! P.S. I got this game as soon as it released, thank you for such an amazing game! It is hard for me to put down!

english.summary: A Touhou-themed roguelike deckbuilder released on Oct 26, 2026, self-developed and self-published by EskiNott Game Studio and filed under Adventure, Casual, Indie, RPG and Strategy. The Steam AI disclosure states that generative AI was used in the games art production for both image creation and image enhancement, and was used to translate the localised content. This site records art and translation as used on that wording and the remaining six areas as areas the disclosure does not address. Every finding rests on the developer own statement and none of it has been independently audited.
english.reviewNote: Checked the complete English Steam AI disclosure, the identity (EskiNott Game Studio is both developer and publisher) and the English discussion homepage (15 visible topics of 15, so the homepage covers every topic), and read both keyword-matched threads in full including every visible reply. In Please remove AI from this game players criticise the visible AI traces and the developer answers under a developer badge that the game is made entirely alone, that their financial situation does not allow commissioning artists or buying better art assets, that AI-generated artwork was a compromise under those limits, and that replacement would be considered if sales allow. In Question for dev, about the extend of the AI art usage players ask which models were used. These are community posts and developer forum statements, recorded here as what those people said rather than as independent verification, and they do not extend any area the disclosure leaves open. This title was searched once, that one response holds 6 results and 2 raw sources were read: the genplay.gg entry and the AI Transparency Index entry both transcribe the store disclosure verbatim. The index page additionally marks the process as AI-generated and live AI during play as No with a model-reported confidence of 95 percent, while stating on the same page that this is auto-classified model output, not an accuracy rate or a human review score, and that the raw disclosure remains the source of truth; this site therefore does not adopt its live-generation finding and keeps that area unaddressed. The remaining 4 results were the store page and a curators-parameter variant of it, a storefront mirror on pcgame.com and a listing page of a deckbuilder subreddit; none carries verifiable information beyond the disclosure, so none is registered as a source.
